citations.description: test_compute_validity_grandfathers_a_real_regver_change (unscoped, no dep lines, no code drift) and test_compute_validity_still_catches_a_real_code_drift (current regver, no registry rotation) — neither is the combined case
test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_other_staleness: rotates registry + head drift (stale-head), not code drift on a scoped attestation
Ticket comment round 2 claims test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_code_drift_on_a_scoped_attestation was added in Gerrit change 967, but the test is not present in the repository

findings.criterion: stale-code, stale-head, stale-material and stale-reopened still return valid: False — proven by a test that rotates the registry AND drifts a dependency file on one attestation and asserts the verdict is stale-code.
findings.detail: The AC requires a single test that simultaneously rotates the registry (uses an old regver) AND drifts a dependency file on a scoped attestation, asserting the verdict is stale-code. No such combined test exists in the codebase. The ticket comment (round 2) claims it was added as test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_code_drift_on_a_scoped_attestation in Gerrit change 967, but that test is absent from tests/unit/test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py and from all other test files. The existing tests cover the two dimensions separately: test_compute_validity_still_catches_a_real_code_drift (lines 369-414) uses the current regver (no rotation) and drifts code; test_compute_validity_grandfathers_a_real_regver_change (lines 345-366) rotates the registry but uses an unscoped attestation with no dep lines (no code drift). test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_other_staleness in test_compute_validity.py (lines 123-137) rotates the registry and drifts HEAD but uses an unscoped attestation (stale-head, not stale-code). None of these is the combined scoped-attestation case the AC specifies.
findings.remediation: Add test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_code_drift_on_a_scoped_attestation to tests/unit/test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py: sign a SCOPED attestation against an old regver AND a dep file, then edit and commit the dep file post-signing, and assert verdict == 'stale-code' with registry_drift populated.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
